Definition: Total pial surface area of the cerebrum from the 3-D MRI surface reconstruction, in square millimetres; species mean of the paper's specimens (Heuer et al. 2019). Whole-cerebrum value, BOTH hemispheres combined: the cortical-areas merge's canonical total surface is per hemisphere, so this variable is housed separately and could join that merge only after halving (curator decision, not done here).
Note: Authors' archive column 'Surface Area' (github.com/neuroanatomy/34primates, data/derived/stats/stats.csv); range across specimens 627-236,309 mm2.

Definition: Volume of the cerebrum from the 3-D MRI surface reconstruction, in cubic millimetres; species mean of the paper's specimens (Heuer et al. 2019). Reconstructed cerebral tissue volume -- not endocranial volume.

Absolute gyrification index (AbsGI) as defined by Heuer et al. (2019): the ratio between the surface area of the cerebral surface reconstruction and the surface area of a sphere of the same volume. A sphere has the minimum value, 1; the authors report about 4 for a human cerebrum. Dimensionless; species mean of the paper's specimens. The archived values are whole-cerebrum values: for the 28 species with one specimen, AbsGI equals Cerebral_surface_area divided by the surface area of a sphere of Cerebral_volume (both hemispheres together), although the paper words the definition for a cerebral hemisphere. NOT the Zilles 2-D coronal-contour GI and never pooled with it, nor with the Mota & Herculano-Houzel folding index (owner decision 2026-07-31).
Note: Authors' archive column 'AbsGI'; range across specimens 1.49-4.50.

Definition: Total folding length as defined by Heuer et al. (2019): the total length of the curves dividing sulci from gyri, measured on a mean-curvature map of the cerebral surface reconstruction, in millimetres; species mean of the paper's specimens. Conceptually similar to the gyral length of Prothero & Sundsten (1984) and the sulcal lengths referenced by Zilles et al. (1989), which were measured on the exposed surface or on endocasts; not pooled with them.

Estimated number of sulci as defined by Heuer et al. (2019): the count of regions of the cerebral surface reconstruction with negative mean curvature; species mean of the paper's specimens, so merged values may be fractional.
Mean fold wavelength (Lambda), in millimetres; species mean of the paper's specimens (Heuer et al. 2019). Approximately constant (~12 mm) across the sample despite a ~20x cerebral-volume range.

Mean fold depth (Delta), in millimetres; species mean of the paper's specimens (Heuer et al. 2019). One specimen (Microcebus murinus, the species' only specimen) carries a small negative published value (-0.0824343); the authors' own analysis scripts clip Delta < 0 to 0, but the value is kept verbatim in this merge, so the Microcebus murinus species value is negative.
Note: Authors' archive column 'Delta'; do not clip at build.
